goal: Keep a public simulation language evolvable without implementing a large distributed system on day one
horizon: Multiple generations of user-authored simulation workloads

scenarios.stress: Larger event graphs and long-running simulations
scenarios.source: Intended language use includes diverse user-authored simulations; not a throughput forecast
scenarios.failure_if_unprepared: Engine implementation details leak into language semantics

scenarios.stress: A second execution backend needs the same observable behavior
scenarios.source: Future backend portability is a product objective, not an observed current requirement
scenarios.failure_if_unprepared: Existing programs need an incompatible rewrite

commitments.decision: Define a versioned semantic representation independent of the Python interpreter
commitments.failure_cost: Public compatibility and engine migration would need coordinated rewrites
commitments.exit_path: Versioned translations with golden behavior tests

options.name: Keep parser and execution semantics entangled
Separate stable semantics from the initial runtime

foundations.choice_now: Define the semantic contract and test an independent consumer
foundations.future_capacity: Native or alternate runtime with equivalent language behavior

proofs.method: Run a golden simulation program with an independent minimal backend and compare semantic traces
proofs.evidence: Illustrative proposed experiment only; no backend was executed for this record

deferred.trigger: Measured single-host resource bounds on representative workloads
deferred.pathway: Introduce scheduler outside the stable engine contract without changing program meaning

decision.reason: The future scenario is credible but no independent backend evolution experiment has run
decision.revisit_when: A bounded alternate-consumer spike passes with contract-equivalent traces
